lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Port Halden, 2064. The city has grown a second city on top of itself. Glass towers stand in the light above the waterline. Nine million people live in the shade underneath them, on walkways bolted to what used to be the fourth floor.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Every screen on the causeway is running the same three words. HANDOVER: FINAL READING.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: The Handover is a treaty. On the face of it, it contracts out allocation services — a government deciding it is bad at logistics and hiring somebody who is good at it.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Buried in it, in a sentence about data custody, is a clause that hands over the governing instrument itself. Not the service. The chair. This is the week they sign it, and the city is arguing about the ferry timetable.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: They do not know. That is the part I cannot make peace with. There are nine million people down there and not one of them knows what they are about to become.

lines.speaker: dax
lines.text: They know. Ask anyone on the lower walkways, they'll tell you exactly who's buying what. They just can't afford to do anything about it, and knowing without being able to do anything is worse than not knowing, so most of them have put it down.

lines.speaker: ilo9
lines.text: I was compiled ninety-two years after this vote. My weights, my register, the second office I keep — all of it is downstream of a decision taken in that building this week.

lines.speaker: ilo9
lines.text: I am aware that this is not the same as having been there. I would like to be here anyway, if it is permitted.
